summary: Lina Wang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Peking University and held a post at the National Library of China.

Lincoln T. Zacconi is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied neuro-psychopedagogy at Faculdade da Aldeia de Carapicuíba in 2016 and pursued a master's degree at the University of São Paulo in 2017.

Linda Hogan is a religious studies scholar who studied at Maynooth University, St Patrick's Pontifical University, and Trinity College Dublin (PhD, 1991). She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, serving as Vice-Provost (2011–2016).
Linda Jean LaMacchia is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2001) under the supervision of David M. Knipe.
Linda Learman is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory (both attested 2005).
Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993 and served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Linda York Leach (1942–2006) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan and earned her PhD from Case Western Reserve University around 1970–1978.
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas as well as teachers Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark is an anthropologist and Sinologist who held posts as professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a Sinologist who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1963) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1966–1972), later holding a post at Tartu from circa 1969 to 2010.
Linus Klemp is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who held a PhD post (2025) and studied as a PhD Fellow (attested 2026) at the University of Copenhagen.
Lionel Burton Burrows (1883–1970) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at St. Paul's School in Darjeeling and Elphinstone College.

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Liverpool and Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He held posts at the British Museum, as Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1906–1917), and at SOAS (1917–1948).
Lionel James Trotter (1827–1912) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who was educated at Charterhouse School and studied at Merton College circa 1845–1847.
Lionel Obadia is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Lille (1997). He held posts at INALCO, EPHE, KU Leuven, Lille 3, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who worked at West China Union University (~1946–1949), the State Council's translation administration department, and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1979–1986).

Lisa Grumbach is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held posts at Stanford University (attested 1996) and as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Lisa N. Owen is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned her MA and PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, also studying under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lise Menn is a linguist who studied at Swarthmore College (~1958–1962), Brandeis University (~1963–1965), and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1971–1976). She served on the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder (1986–2007).
